taxonomic_note: Current Kew/POWO accepted species concept. Historical Verbena combinations remain useful search aliases in sources.
look_here_first: LOOK AT A MATURE LEAF: low or pink mock vervain has small, broadly ovate-to-triangular leaves (ca. 12–27 mm) with 3–6 pairs of comparatively broad fan-shaped primary lobes, often with secondary notches. Then inspect the very small flowers and the terminal spike: even in FRUIT the spike axis scarcely elongates.

project_inclusion.range_basis: South-central Texas floristic voucher set explicitly records G. pumila in Uvalde, Medina, and Real counties; Travis and Williamson are also independently documented.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Exact county voucher evidence; no inferred counties.

best_field_traits: annual, low and spreading to ascending
often under 20 cm tall in Williamson material
small broadly ovate leaves with 3–6 paired lobes and sublobes
young foliage velvety with nonglandular and stalked glandular hairs
inflorescence axis does not strongly elongate in fruit
morphology_keys.comparison_training: G. bipinnatifida has larger, more deeply and finely 1–2-pinnately dissected leaves and generally a coarser, more feathery appearance. G. pumila is the smaller, compact, broad-lobed plant.
morphology_keys.habit: Small annual, commonly low/spreading or ascending, in Williamson County specimens up to ~19 cm; stems square/4-angled, often hairy with stalked glandular hairs.
morphology_keys.leaf_arrangement: Opposite, often decussate; short petioles and broad, more or less triangular/ovate blade outline.
morphology_keys.leaf_dissected: Mature leaves commonly 12–27 mm in outline, with 3–6 pairs of broad, fan-like primary lobes and shallow-to-moderate secondary divisions; appearance is chunkier and less feathery than typical G. bipinnatifida.
morphology_keys.flowering_structure: Dense short terminal spike, typically about 25 mm long in flowering Williamson material, with small pale-purple/pink flowers; rachis does NOT elongate materially in fruit.
morphology_keys.flower_measurements: Flower limb about 7–8 mm across (UT Williamson); Flower corolla tube ~4–5 mm plus throat ~2–3 mm; North Central Texas key gives corolla tube roughly 8–10 mm depending on measurement convention. Do not mix tube-only and tube-plus-throat numbers.
morphology_keys.fruit: Four mericarps, each roughly 2.5 × 0.7 mm in regional material, persistent calyx; fruiting axis stays relatively compact.
field_checks: Look for SMALL, broad, coarsely lobed leaves rather than featherlike leaves.
Compare same-position mature leaves against G. bipinnatifida.
Check little pink flowers and a SHORT fruiting axis; flower color alone is weak.
Use calyx/flower close-up to confirm when leaf form overlaps.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Compared with G. bipinnatifida: often distinctly smaller, broadly triangular/ovate leaves with fewer fan-shaped major lobes and sublobes, not the larger deeply once/twice-pinnate featherlike pattern; spike remains short and compact even as fruit matures. Stature and pink-purple color overlap; neither suffices alone.

cross_genus_lookalikes.difference: Both can be low, hairy, and pink/purple flowering; V. canescens has gray canescent foliage and more slender flower spikes, rather than a dense compact Glandularia head and broad fan-lobed leaf.

V. halei often has very deeply divided lower leaves but narrow upper leaves and elongate slender spikes, whereas G. pumila is a low compact plant with small broadly lobed leaves and a short persistent head.
